title: 詩意的畫  苦寂的心
source: 詩意的畫  苦寂的心.docx

flow.zh:
詩意的畫   苦寂的心
  -- 看梵谷畫展有感 --

flow.caption_zh:
今晨坐電車
來美術館看你的畫
主題是： Van Gogh at work

zh: 眼前掠過的是圖畫景物
腳下踩著的是你的人生歷程
牽映出多少觀者的自我
所有無法詮釋的色調語氣？
en: What flashes past before my eyes is a painted scene
A pastoral melody, gentle as poetry
A dazzling, dreamlike night sky of stars
What lies beneath your feet is the course of your life
Your passion, your struggle
Your sorrow and despair
The pulse stirred up by strokes of color
Reflecting how much of each viewer's own self
If viewing a painting is also a dialogue
Then how am I to keep asking
All the tones and shades that cannot be explained?

zh: 不是自戀式的表情張揚
另有一番無人訴說的寂寞
en: Having seen many of your self-portraits
It isn't a self-loving display of expression
It is the outpouring of inner emotion
There is a fierce, disdainful pride
There is self-injury, self-abandonment
Or thick hair and a heavy beard
Or with weary eyes half-closed
A bald brow and sagging jaw, decay
A face of sickly green and faded yellow
It is a turning point of the heart's path
It is the transformation of form and shape
A face weathered by wind and frost
Like the weathered age of a tree
There is yet another loneliness no one speaks of
Only I cannot see that face of yours after you cut off your ear
The sorrow of a wound wrapped in bandages

zh: 對現實徹底絕望的抉擇？
en: Pausing before your final painting
"Wheatfield with Crows"
The wheat field in the painting brims with gold
A muddy path winds through the fields
A sky where crows beat their wings
Gloomy and oppressive, haunted by demons and specters
I ponder to myself
Facing a blank canvas
How you agonized in thought
Which color is it, after all
One can depict
Wheat field, vast sky, slanting light
A clamoring flock of crows
A tense standoff spanning heaven and earth
To express the loneliness of a broken heart
8 attached to a backpack; and
A choice born of utter despair at reality?

zh: 依然是梵谷苦寂的心情
en: Walking out of the art museum
By the streets of Amsterdam
August sunlight scattered across the ground
Spreading out a sky of pure blue
The art book says
The cloud-swept wheat fields of Auvers
As if the face of long ago
Still Van Gogh's bitter, lonely state of mind

points.zh: 梵谷是一位感情激動的畫家，一生充滿愛和熱情，充滿矛盾和悲劇。梵谷早期雖受荷蘭古畫和印象畫的影響，但其時代背景正是象徵主義崛起之時，象徵主義是用色彩與形體來解釋，並喚起各種隱藏的靈性。明暗的對比、跳躍的色彩，是近代詩文藝術的一個共同情緒。梵谷的強烈個人特質，在畫作上完全釋放出來，鮮明的色彩和蠕動漩渦狀的燃燒筆觸，對象適當的變形，濃厚的主觀見解。不僅傾注精神和感情於畫作上，更強調色彩之美和藝術表現的象徵意義，也因而啟示了二十世紀藝術的主題，即根本的「純粹性」。
points.en: Van Gogh was a painter of intense feeling, whose life was filled with love and passion, contradiction and tragedy. Although Van Gogh's early work was influenced by the old Dutch masters and Impressionism, his era was also the time when Symbolism was rising — Symbolism sought to use color and form to interpret and evoke various hidden spiritual states. Contrasts of light and dark, and leaping colors, were a shared emotional undercurrent in modern poetry and art. Van Gogh's intense personal character was fully unleashed in his paintings — vivid colors, writhing, whirlpool-like burning brushstrokes, appropriately distorted subjects, and strong subjective vision. He poured not only spirit and emotion into his paintings but also emphasized the beauty of color and the symbolic significance of artistic expression, and in doing so foreshadowed the central theme of twentieth-century art: fundamental "purity."

points.zh: 梵谷在奧維爾 ( Auvers-sur-Oise ) 繪作的「麥田群鴉」( Wheat Field with Crows ) ，一般認為是他最後的作品。金黃的麥田，暗沉的天空，延向天際的田間泥路，被他畫筆一揮截斷：讓人間豐收，讓自己無路吧！就在麥田草堆邊，他收起畫筆， 折起畫架，然後……舉槍穿胸。沒人知道他是如何負傷回到他的居屋閣樓，他的弟弟希歐趕到，在床邊守候兩天，梵谷才溘然長逝。時為1890年的7月，三十七歲的英年。如今，奧維爾的村郊，梵谷兄弟的粗簡墓碑，相依併列。
points.en: Van Gogh's painting 'Wheatfield with Crows,' painted at Auvers-sur-Oise, is generally considered his final work. The golden wheatfield, the dark, brooding sky, the dirt path stretching toward the horizon — all cut off abruptly by his brush, as if to say: let the human world reap its harvest, let there be no path left for himself. There, by the haystacks at the edge of the wheatfield, he put down his brush, folded up his easel, and then... shot himself in the chest. No one knows how he managed, wounded, to make his way back to his attic room; his brother Theo rushed to his side and kept watch for two days before Van Gogh quietly passed away. It was July 1890, at the young age of thirty-seven. Today, on the outskirts of the village of Auvers, the simple gravestones of the Van Gogh brothers lie side by side.
